english_translation: The Zambezi River lies on the border between Zimbabwe and Zambia.

dialogue.english: The Zambezi River lies on the border between Zimbabwe and Zambia.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Rwizi [river] • rweZambezi [rwezambezi] • rwuripamuganhu [rwuripamuganhu] • peZimbabwe [pezimbabwe] • neZambia [and / with zambia]

grammar_notes.title: Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'neZambia'
grammar_notes.content: Look closely at 'neZambia'. In Shona, the word for 'and' or 'with' between nouns is not a separate word—instead, the prefix 'ne-' (or 'na-' before people's names) is written attached directly to the second noun! For example, 'ne-' + 'Zambia' forms 'neZambia'. You will see this everywhere in daily speech: 'sadza nemuriwo' ('sadza and vegetables'), 'nesimba' ('with strength'), and 'nekukasira' ('with haste / quickly').
grammar_notes.rule: ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

grammar_notes.title: How Shona Sentences Fit Together (Subject + Tense + Verb)
grammar_notes.content: In 'Rwizi rweZambezi rwuripamuganhu peZimbabwe neZambia', notice how a single Shona verb word packs together who is doing the action (the subject prefix), when it happens (the tense marker), and the action itself (the verb stem). Once you recognize the building blocks at the start of the verb—like 'ndi-' (I), 'u-' (you), 'ti-' (we), or 'va-' (they)—you can immediately spot the subject even when no separate pronoun word is used!
grammar_notes.rule: [Who (Subject Prefix)] + [When (Tense Marker)] + [Action (Verb Root)] -> e.g., ti- (we) + -cha- (will) + -svika (arrive) = tichasvika

grammar_notes.title: Describing Nouns: Word Order in Shona
grammar_notes.content: In English, descriptive words like adjectives, possessives ('my', 'our'), demonstratives ('this', 'that'), and numbers come BEFORE the noun ('this big house', 'my two books'). In Shona, the noun always comes FIRST, and all descriptive words follow right after it! For example: 'nyama iyi' ('this meat'), 'mwana uyu' ('this child'), 'goho guru' ('a big harvest'), and 'makomo marefu' ('tall mountains').
grammar_notes.rule: Noun FIRST + Descriptor SECOND -> mota iyi (this car), mabhuku edu (our books), makomo marefu (tall mountains)

cultural_notes.title: The Mighty Zambezi River ('Rwizi rweZambezi') & Victoria Falls ('Mosi-oa-Tunya')
cultural_notes.content: Forming the entire northern border between Zimbabwe and Zambia ('pamuganhu peZimbabwe neZambia'), the Zambezi River plunges over Victoria Falls ('Mosi-oa-Tunya' / 'Mapopoma eVictoria') and fills Lake Kariba, one of the world's largest man-made lakes.

active_exercises.prompt: How do you say 'Tall trees and green grass' in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Miti mirefu' = 'tall trees' (plural 'mi-' agreement on '-refu'), and 'neuswa hwegirinhi' = 'and green grass'.
